It originates and services short-term bridging finance, property development finance, buy-to-let and residential mortgages for UK intermediaries, brokers, property developers, landlords and investors, and runs a parallel capital business that lets individual, corporate and institutional investors put money into secured UK property loans. The company distributes almost entirely through mortgage intermediaries via its Mortgages Portal, and was the first UK fintech to securitise its own buy-to-let loan book. LendInvest publishes no public developer API, developer portal or SDKs; its broker and borrower integrations run through hosted portals rather than a documented public API surface.

providers.name: Lumin Digital
providers.description: Lumin Digital is a cloud-native digital banking platform for credit unions and community banks, founded in 2016 by Jeff Chambers and headquartered in San Ramon, California. The platform is built on a single-tenant, microservices architecture and sits on top of an institution's existing core banking processor, delivering retail banking, commercial banking, digital account opening, user engagement, risk management, digital marketing and data analytics as modules. Its extensibility layer is API- and SDK-based: Lumin publishes a client SDK and a partner API programme that connects the platform to a stated 200+ third-party fintech solutions, and a developer portal used by financial institutions and integration partners to move data into and out of digital banking. The API reference, SDK downloads and developer portal are reachable only through the authenticated client portal at clients.lumindigital.com, so no machine-readable contract is published publicly.

providers.name: Upstart
providers.description: Upstart is an AI lending marketplace (NASDAQ: UPST) that connects consumers with banks and credit unions, using AI-driven underwriting models to price credit beyond traditional FICO-based scoring. The marketplace offers personal loans, car loan refinancing, debt consolidation, home equity lines of credit, and short-term relief loans - loans are originated by regulated bank and credit-union partners, including lender-branded powered-by-Upstart sites. Upstart's API surface is partner-facing rather than public: a Reporting API for lending partners is operated at api.upstart.com and publicly tracked on status.upstart.com, but no public developer portal or API documentation is published.

providers.name: Xoom
providers.description: Xoom is PayPal's international money transfer (remittance) service, operating since 2001. Consumers use Xoom to send money to bank accounts, debit cards, mobile wallets, UPI, and PIX, send cash for pickup or delivery, and reload mobile phones in countries around the world, with up-front fees and exchange rates. U.S. transfers are provided by PayPal, Inc., a licensed money transmitter; UK/EEA service is provided by PayPal (Europe) S.a r.l., regulated by the Luxembourg CSSF. Xoom is a consumer service and publishes no public developer API on the xoom.com domain.

providers.name: AvidXchange
providers.description: AvidXchange is a fintech provider of AI-powered accounts payable (AP) and payment automation software for middle-market businesses. Its platform digitizes invoice capture, approval workflows, purchase orders, and supplier payments, integrating with more than 220 accounting and ERP systems and connecting buyers to a large supplier network for paperless, straight-through AP processing. AvidXchange publishes a partner and integration developer portal (ReadMe-hosted) for connecting ERP systems and building against its payment and invoice automation platform; the API reference is gated behind partner login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, QED Investors, and Sapphire Ventures and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Kapital
providers.description: Kapital (KPTL MEXICO BANK, S.A., Institucion de Banca Multiple, Kapital Mexico Grupo Financiero) is a licensed Mexican bank and AI-native financial platform for SMEs and corporates, founded in 2019 and headquartered in Mexico City. Its ecosystem combines business and personal deposit accounts, corporate cards, SPEI and SPID transfers, FX cash/transfers/cheques and derivatives (forwards, interest rates), working-capital and revolving credit (Credito Empresarial, Credito PyME, Credito FLEX), factoring, and fixed-income investments (Pagare, CEDES) with Kapital IA, a native artificial-intelligence layer that reconciles cash flow, projects sales, validates supplier pricing and flags anomalous costs. It is supervised by the CNBV and Banco de Mexico, with deposits protected by IPAB, and it also operates in Colombia as Kapital Colombia. Kapital publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK or webhook surface; the banking surface is delivered through its own web and mobile applications.

providers.name: Miter
providers.description: Miter is a Human Capital Management (HCM) platform purpose-built for construction contractors, consolidating payroll, HR, benefits, field operations, and expense management into a single connected system. Its construction payroll automates prevailing-wage, certified-payroll, and union compliance, multi-state tax handling, and fully-burdened job-cost tracking in real time, while its HRIS covers recruiting, benefits, performance, and learning. Field Operations adds time tracking, scheduling, daily reports, production tracking, and safety, and Expense Management handles reimbursements, per diems, and corporate cards. Miter connects to construction ERPs and accounting systems (Sage Intacct, NetSuite, Acumatica, QuickBooks, Procore, Viewpoint, and more) through off-the-shelf integrations or a custom REST API. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Anduin Transactions
providers.description: Anduin builds digital fund operations software for private markets, serving venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform streamlines investor onboarding and fund administration through products including Fund Subscription, Data Room, Investor Data Management, Engagement Hub, Integration Hub, a Data Extraction Service, and Investor Access/Portal. Anduin reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this record captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance program for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Constantinople
providers.description: Constantinople is a Sydney-based fintech providing an AI-native core-banking platform that lets banks run product, technology, data, operations, and compliance as a single modern fabric. It powers retail, business, and embedded banking across accounts, payments, cards, lending, mortgages, and term deposits, with headless APIs and SDKs, digital onboarding, an AI concierge for customers, and the "Justinian" AI workbench for bankers. Risk and compliance (fraud, financial-crime detection, regulatory reporting) are built into the platform, which is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. Constantinople is backed by Prosus Ventures (Series A, A$50M). The developer/API surface is a gated B2B platform; enrichment here is sourced from the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Hummingbird
providers.description: Hummingbird is an AI-powered compliance operations platform for financial institutions and fintechs. It automates customer screening (sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media checks), transaction monitoring for financial crime, investigations and case management, and regulatory reporting including automated SAR, STR, and CTR filing. Hummingbird orchestrates risk and anti-money-laundering (AML) workflows across a connected app marketplace of 50+ integrations, and exposes custom two-way integration APIs provisioned through its partnerships team. The company is SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified and backed by Homebrew.

providers.name: Coast
providers.description: Coast is a fintech company providing a unified payments platform for fleet-based and field-service businesses, combining a smart Visa fuel card, corporate card, field card, and bill pay into a single program with granular spending controls, GPS- and tank-capacity-based fraud prevention, fuel rebates, and a fraud guarantee. Coast operates a stable v2 REST API (the Coast API) behind a developer portal that lets businesses programmatically access cards, drivers, vehicles, transactions, receipts, and controls, alongside native integrations with telematics (Samsara, Geotab, Verizon Connect), accounting (QuickBooks, NetSuite, Sage Intacct), and fleet management (Fleetio, Whip Around) platforms. Coast is backed by Accel and ICONIQ Capital.

providers.name: Debitura
providers.description: Debitura is an API-first international debt collection platform covering cross-border B2B and B2C receivables. It publishes three separate public REST APIs, one per role in the network rather than one API with role-gated endpoints: the Customer API for creditors uploading invoices to collection and tracking cases, the Referral Partner API for platforms embedding collection as a referral and tracking revenue share, and the Collection Partner API for collection agencies operating cases on the platform. All three are OpenAPI 3.0.4, each on its own host, and each authenticates with an API key in the XApiKey header; the Customer API additionally accepts a bearer token, and the Referral Partner API exposes OAuth operations for minting them. Webhooks appear in all three, each with a paired test surface for exercising events before going live. Debitura publishes its own APIs.json at docs.debitura.com, which is how this profile was built.

providers.name: helios
providers.description: helios is a French sustainable-banking company (HELIOS SAS, Paris) offering current, Premium, joint, youth, Liberté and independent/professional accounts, a green savings passbook, sustainable life insurance and wooden or recycled-plastic Visa cards through iOS, Android and web. It is a société à mission and a certified B Corp whose promise is that no customer euro finances fossil fuels or polluting industry, and it publishes the list of transition projects it funds. helios is registered in REGAFI under 731225 as a payment services agent of OKALI, the ACPR-approved electronic money institution that services the accounts. It publishes no public API, SDK, webhook or developer portal; the one machine-readable document it serves is an llms.txt AI-usage policy.

providers.name: Mantle
providers.description: Mantle is an AI-powered data platform for alternative assets management, positioning itself as "alternative assets data, structured for the agentic era." It offers two products: Mantle Equity, a cap table management platform for founders and CFOs covering fundraising, SAFEs, stock options, 409A valuations, and QSBS attestation; and Mantle Portal, a portfolio management and insights product for institutional investors such as endowments and family offices. Mantle converts fragmented documents into structured, trustworthy data and layers AI workflows on top. The company is SOC 2 Type II compliant and is backed by Sierra Ventures. As of this enrichment pass no public developer API or API documentation was found; the product is delivered as a hosted SaaS application with an end-user help center.

providers.name: LiqPay
providers.description: LiqPay is a Ukrainian payment platform operated by PrivatBank that provides REST APIs for accepting card payments, creating hosted payment pages, processing subscriptions, managing refunds, sending invoices, and conducting card-to-card transfers. It supports Mastercard, Visa, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Privat24 wallets across 120+ countries, with full fiscalization (RRO) support for Ukrainian merchants.

providers.name: Tiptop
providers.description: Tiptop (Tiptop Labs) is the payments company founded by Postmates co-founder Bastian Lehmann that lets shoppers trade in items they already own for instant credit at checkout, alongside pay-over-time options. Merchants integrate through a Shopify payments app, a Salesforce Commerce Cloud cartridge, a Magento 2 module, or the Direct API — the tiptop.js browser library plus server-side order-management endpoints (capture, void, refund) authenticated with an api-key header. Backed by a16z ($23M Series A, 2022). Note: as of July 2026 tiptop.com redirects to mother.ai (Mother Computer Inc.) and its TLS certificate has expired, while docs.tiptop.com, api.tiptop.com, cdn.tiptop.com, and the first-party packages remain live.

providers.name: Vanilla
providers.description: Vanilla (Vanilla Technologies Inc.) is an estate planning platform for financial advisors, RIAs, and wealth management firms. The platform provides AI-powered estate document analysis and estate health assessments, estate visualization, scenario modeling for tax strategies, and estate document creation, letting advisors deliver estate planning across clients at all wealth levels. Vanilla is SOC 2 Type II audited and integrates with wealth management platforms including Salesforce, Orion, Black Diamond, Addepar, eMoney, and Plaid. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer portal or API documentation is published; the api.justvanilla.com host is private.

providers.name: Pascal AI
providers.description: Pascal AI (Pascal AI Labs) is an institutional-finance AI company building context-driven, MCP-native research agents that turn enterprise and market data into investment insights for hedge funds, asset managers, investment banks, and private-markets firms. Pascal sits inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word, email, and the browser through an Agent Control Center, ships 25+ pre-built research agents, maintains a persistent knowledge graph and memory across every document a team has touched, and returns fully cited outputs with RBAC enforcement. It deploys inside the customer VPC or on-premises and exposes an enterprise API & SDK (Python, TypeScript, REST) plus finance-ready MCP connectors. Founded in 2024 in Bangalore, Pascal AI raised a $3.1M seed round in 2025 led by Kalaari Capital with Norwest Venture Partners, Antler, and Info Edge Ventures. It publishes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR compliance. No public API specification or developer portal is published; developer surfaces are gated to enterprise customers.

providers.name: Ready (formerly Argent)
providers.description: Ready (formerly Argent) is a self-custodial crypto wallet and smart-account platform for Starknet and Ethereum. It builds account-abstraction wallets (Ready Wallet, Ready Multisig, Web Wallet), the Ready Card for cashing out, and developer tooling for dApps — session keys, paymasters / gas abstraction, outside execution, multicalls, and signature/cosigner verification — shipped as first-party client SDKs (StarknetKit, @argent/x-sessions, web3.swift, starknet.swift). The company rebranded from Argent to Ready; developer resources live at docs.ready.co and the argentlabs GitHub organization. Its developer surface is client SDKs rather than a public REST API.

providers.name: Symmetrical
providers.description: Symmetrical.ai is a Polish-British HR and payroll fintech, founded in 2019 in Warsaw with offices in London and Barcelona and backed by Partech. It provides payroll and HR bureau outsourcing plus an HR platform automating wage calculation, digital document management, onboarding, leave and time tracking, and real-time analytics, alongside employee financial wellbeing tools such as earned-wage / salary-on-demand access. Symmetrical is ISO/IEC 27001 certified. The company operates an authentication-gated developer documentation portal (developer.symmetrical.ai) but publishes no public OpenAPI, API reference, or SDKs; this profile captures its public identity plus probed security posture.

providers.name: Remitly
providers.description: Remitly is a Seattle-based digital financial services provider for immigrants and their families, operating a global cross-border remittance and money-movement network across more than 170 countries. Beyond its consumer money-transfer app, Remitly runs "Remitly for Developers" (Remitly Access), a gated enterprise partner API that lets businesses embed international payouts, cross-border payments, and locally relevant disbursement options into their own products, along with open-source "Connected Experiences" mobile/web SDK components. Remitly is a regulated money services business: FinCEN-registered, licensed as a money transmitter across all 50 U.S. states, and registered with FINTRAC in Canada. Added to the API Evangelist network as a fintech company profile and enriched with identity, domain-security, and compliance artifacts.

providers.name: Sunlight
providers.description: Sunlight is an educational-spending platform that lets organizations fund learning for their people. Administrators create groups, invite registered or unregistered members, allocate a per-user education budget ("sunlight"), and let members place orders for courses, books and subscriptions from providers such as Amazon and Platzi, while an activity feed tracks what members join and buy. Its REST API is built on the JSON:API specification (media type application/vnd.api+json) with Bearer-token authentication, and exposes groups, group membership and invitations, per-user credit/budget transactions, orders, and activities. Sunlight was backed by Seedcamp and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Tide
providers.description: Tide is a UK business finance and administration platform ("built by business owners for business owners") serving over two million small businesses, sole traders, freelancers, and limited companies. It combines a business current account (an e-money account powered by ClearBank), expense cards, invoicing and payment tools (Tap to Pay, card readers, QR codes, payment links), MTD-ready accounting and admin, business credit and finance (loans, asset finance, invoice finance), company formation, and business insurance. Tide is authorised and regulated in relation to its regulated activities by the UK Financial Conduct Authority. Tide was surfaced as a portfolio company of Anthemis, Creandum, and Speedinvest. It does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; "Open Banking" is offered as a consumer product feature.

providers.name: Neo.Tax
providers.description: Neo.Tax is an AI-powered tax automation platform that helps enterprises and their accounting teams generate audit-ready R&D tax credit studies, software capitalization (ASC 350-40), and R&D capitalization (IRC Section 174) documentation. The platform ingests engineering and financial data from tools like Jira, GitHub, payroll systems, and Workday and uses large language models and agentic AI to qualify projects under IRC Section 41, eliminating the manual surveys and interviews that traditionally drive R&D tax credit work. Neo.Tax is backed by GV and Uncork Capital and delivered as a closed enterprise SaaS product; it operates a customer application, a help center, a public status page, and a trust center (SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR) but does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: EarnUp
providers.description: EarnUp is a San Francisco-based financial-wellness fintech that automates consumer debt paydown and savings. Using patented technology and predictive analytics, its platform lets people schedule and automatically make payments toward mortgages, auto loans, student loans, and other personal debt, and save for life events. EarnUp sells engagement and AI-advisor tooling to lenders, mortgage servicers, credit unions, employers, unions, and financial professionals, and reports that more than three million people have used the platform. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bain Capital Ventures, this is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; EarnUp publishes no public developer API, so enrichment is limited to identity and security posture.

providers.name: Fundbox
providers.description: Fundbox is an API-first embedded working capital platform that enables B2B sellers and platforms to offer net payment terms, credit underwriting, and working capital financing. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Plano, TX, Fundbox has unlocked over $6 billion in capital for more than 170,000 small businesses. The platform provides a fully white-labeled, embedded lending API stack that allows B2B platforms to integrate credit decisioning, compliance, and servicing in two weeks or less.

providers.name: Lively
providers.description: Lively is a fintech-healthtech company that provides modern, cloud-based Health Savings Accounts (HSA) alongside Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), Health Reimbursement Arrangements (HRA), COBRA, and commuter benefits for individuals, families, employers, benefits administrators, and third-party administrators. Lively pairs interest-bearing and investment-enabled HSAs (via a Schwab Health Savings Brokerage Account and a guided HSA portfolio) with an employer dashboard for contributions and administration, positioning itself around transparent, zero-hidden-fee pricing. Backed by Costanoa Ventures and GGV Capital, Lively integrates with benefit administration platforms and third-party administrators but does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; integration is handled through its sales and partnerships channels. This profile was surfaced as a VC-portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Lively's public web surface.

providers.name: Obligate
providers.description: Obligate (formerly FQX) is a Swiss digital-securities infrastructure provider for regulated on-chain debt capital markets. Its AssetOS platform lets companies issue tokenized bonds and short-term notes as blockchain-based eNotes and eTrackers under the Swiss DLT Act and Code of Obligations, while institutional investors access regulated on-chain private credit, asset-backed securities and trade-finance yield products. Obligate automates the bond lifecycle with smart contracts across multiple blockchains, with built-in KYB/KYC, settlement and enforcement, reducing issuance cost and time versus traditional debt issuance.

providers.name: Behavox
providers.description: Behavox is an AI-native compliance and conduct-surveillance software company serving the world's leading financial institutions and regulated enterprises. Its Unified AI Controls Platform spans directive, preventive, detective, and corrective controls — including Quantum (voice and text communication surveillance across 50+ languages and 150+ channels), Polaris (trade surveillance), Falcon (insider-threat and human-risk detection), Compass (conflicts of interest and personal account dealing), Atlas (control-room enforcement), Pathfinder (regulatory-change-to-policy), Intelligent Archive, Digital Employees, and Mosaic front-office revenue intelligence. Behavox is backed by Index Ventures and the SoftBank Vision Fund. The company sells directly to enterprise financial-services customers and does not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Binocs
providers.description: Binocs is an agentic AI-powered due diligence and strategic advisory platform for financial professionals — private equity, consulting, corporates and portfolio companies spanning private credit, venture capital and venture debt. The SaaS product (app.binocs.co) automates deal sourcing and screening, investment memos and market assessment, financial statement analysis, growth strategy and pricing diagnostics, CRM integration, and sell-side documentation (CIM, teasers), promising decision-ready diligence in minutes at up to 90% lower cost than traditional consulting. Binocs is an Accel portfolio company with offices in Jersey City, NJ and Bengaluru, India. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation.

providers.name: Greenlight
providers.description: Greenlight is a family-focused financial technology company offering a debit card and mobile banking app built for parents, kids, and teens. The platform pairs parental controls, allowance and chore automation, savings goals, and investing (from $1) with financial-literacy education. Greenlight is a financial technology company, not a bank; banking services are provided through partner banks such as Community Federal Savings Bank. It is backed by a16z and Bond Capital. Greenlight publishes no public developer API or developer portal; this profile captures the company's public identity, security/compliance posture, and trust surface.

providers.name: Invoice2go
providers.description: Invoice2go (part of BILL) is a mobile-first invoicing and small-business management platform for freelancers, contractors, and self-employed professionals. It lets users create and send professional invoices and estimates, accept online payments via bank transfer, credit and debit card, and PayPal, track expenses and billable time, capture customer reviews, and view business reports across web, iOS, and Android. Serving roughly 225,000 small-business users, Invoice2go focuses on getting paid faster and simplifying back-office admin. It was acquired by BILL in 2021. There is no live public developer API; third-party integrations are delivered through an Apideck-powered integrations marketplace (QuickBooks, Xero, MYOB, HubSpot, Shopify, Zapier, and more).

providers.name: Jump – Advisor AI
providers.description: Jump is an AI operating system for financial advisors, used by 35,000+ advisors and ranked #1 across T3, Kitces, and The Oasis Group reports. It organizes its capabilities into three products — Meet (AI notetaker, pre-meeting prep, agendas, automatic follow-ups, and scheduling), Grow (opportunity signals, playbooks, scorecards, surveys, and dashboards), and Operate (AI Associate, unified client profiles, and email assistance) — built on a unified data, integration, and agentic AI orchestration foundation. Jump is integration-led rather than a public-API provider: it ships 39+ two-way integrations with CRMs (Salesforce, Wealthbox, Redtail, HubSpot, AdvisorEngine), financial planning tools (eMoney, RightCapital, Asset-Map), portfolio management (Orion, Black Diamond), custodians (Charles Schwab), and meeting/VoIP platforms (Zoom, Teams, Google Meet, RingCentral), pushing compliance-ready records straight into advisors' systems of record. Backed by Insight Partners. No public developer API or portal is published as of this profile.

providers.name: LiveFlow
providers.description: LiveFlow is an agentic accounting and FP&A platform that connects accounting systems such as QuickBooks and Xero to real-time financial reporting, consolidation, and forecasting. Its Flow product automates month-end close, reconciliation, accounts-receivable management, and journal entries across multiple entities, while LiveFlow FP&A automates consolidation, reporting, and forecasting on a company's existing systems. The platform targets complex, multi-location businesses in construction, healthcare, food & beverage, and retail. LiveFlow is backed by Seedcamp.

providers.name: MFellows
providers.description: Money Fellows (moneyfellows.com) is an Egyptian fintech that digitizes the traditional rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA, or "gam'eya") into app-based "money circles." Over 8 million users save collectively and access payouts and credit through flexible 6, 10, or 12-month circles, with loan amounts up to 1,200,000 EGP, plus a cashback debit card and goal-based savings. The company is regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt and backed by 500 Global. Money Fellows is a consumer (B2C) mobile-first product and publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal; the only machine-discoverable surface on the domain is the Umbraco CMS OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 member-auth server that backs the marketing website. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Beem
providers.description: Beem is a consumer fintech mobile app (trybeem.com) offering instant cash advances of up to $1,000 through its Everdraft feature with no credit check and no interest, alongside personal loans up to $100,000, high-yield savings accounts paying up to 5% APY, AI-powered budgeting, credit building, cashback rewards, identity-theft protection, and insurance products. It supports non-traditional income (gig, freelance, government benefits) and can transfer funds to Cash App or a bank account. Backed by Techstars and used by more than five million people, Beem is consumer-facing and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time. Added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: Jeeves
providers.description: Jeeves is a global financial platform for cross-border businesses, combining corporate cards (physical and virtual with spend controls and cashback), automated expense management with approval flows and policy enforcement, cross-border payments and transfers to 150+ countries in 40+ currencies, instant and stablecoin-based settlement, non-dilutive corporate credit, and AI-driven spend insights. Jeeves operates across Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, Canada, the USA, the UK, and the European Union, serving globally operating companies. Backed by a16z and CRV, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API or documentation surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Marlo Technologies
providers.description: Marlo is a maritime ERP platform for dry bulk, tanker, and commercial shipping companies, unifying chartering, voyage management, finance, banking, and compliance in a single system. Operators use Marlo to plan charters, track voyage operations and cargo, model voyage P&L and cashflow, run valuations and credit scoring, manage loans and covenants, hold multi-currency accounts with FX transfers and corporate cards, and handle sanctions screening, emissions tracking, and CII rating management. Marlo is a Techstars-backed company and holds SOC 2 (AICPA) certification. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass the company exposes a customer web application (app.marlo.co) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: DolarApp
providers.description: DolarApp — rebranded to ARQ in March 2026 — is a Latin American cross-border fintech founded in Mexico in 2022 by former Revolut operators Fernando Terres, Zach Garman and Alvaro Correa. It gives consumers and businesses in Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Brazil digital dollar (USDc) and euro (EURc) accounts, US ACH/wire receiving details, international cards accepted in 180+ countries, interbank-rate FX conversion, bulk supplier and contractor payouts, corporate cards with spend controls, and investment and credit products. It reports roughly two million users and is backed by Sequoia Capital, Founders Fund, Brevan Howard Digital, Y Combinator and Kaszek. DolarApp/ARQ runs a private API host at api.dolarapp.com for its own mobile and web applications but publishes no public developer program, documentation or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: IEX
providers.description: IEX Group, Inc. operates IEX Exchange, a U.S. national securities exchange for equities founded to make trading fairer and more transparent, along with IEX Options (coming soon). IEX is known for its Speed Bump, the IEX Signal, and the D-Limit order type. Its developer- and data-facing surface is market data and connectivity rather than a public REST API: real-time depth-of-book and top-of-book feeds (DEEP+, DEEP, and TOPS, plus their SNAP variants) are distributed over the binary IEX Transport Protocol (IEX-TP v1), with published feed specifications, downloadable historical PCAP samples, and market statistics. Data access is arranged through a Data Subscriber Agreement and direct or third-party connectivity. Sector: fintech / financial markets infrastructure. Backed by Bain Capital Ventures, ICONIQ Capital, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures.

providers.name: Integral
providers.description: Integral (Integral Development Corp.) is a technology provider for institutional currency and digital-asset trading. Its cloud-native, API-first platform delivers liquidity aggregation, execution management, pricing engines, distribution, risk management, settlement, and market data across foreign exchange, CFDs, precious metals, and crypto. Integral serves banks, institutional and retail brokers, precious-metals businesses, and crypto trading firms, and is SOC 2 Type II certified with connectivity over FIX, ITCH, and proprietary REST and WebSocket APIs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel, Electric Capital, and General Catalyst.

providers.name: Juni
providers.description: Juni is a Swedish fintech (headquartered in Göteborg, founded 2020) that provides a financial platform for ecommerce and digital businesses: business banking with multi-currency accounts, corporate and virtual cards, local and global payments, spend management, working-capital financing, and AI-driven accounting with integrations such as Fortnox. Juni is a licensed payment institution under the oversight of the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (SFSA) and is backed by EQT Ventures. It exposes a regulatory PSD2 / Open Banking (ASPSP) API surface for third-party providers, but publishes no public product API, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Maxwell Financial
providers.description: Maxwell is an end-to-end mortgage-origination technology and services company serving banks, independent mortgage banks, and credit unions. Its platform spans a customizable borrower Point of Sale, a Lender Hub for loan officers (pipeline, application processing, document validation, underwriting, and pricing), Business Intelligence analytics, and outsourced services including Maxwell Fulfillment (processing, underwriting, closing), Maxwell Diligence (QC and due diligence), and Private Label Origination. The product is a hosted SaaS delivered through login-gated lender and borrower hubs with a public documentation hub; it does not publish an open, versioned developer API.

providers.name: Calypso
providers.description: APIs and developer resources for Nasdaq Calypso (formerly Adenza / Calypso Technology), a cross-asset front-to-back capital markets technology platform for trading, risk management, collateral, treasury, processing, and accounting used by banks, asset managers, central banks, and clearing houses worldwide.

providers.name: Flowdesk
providers.description: Flowdesk is a full-service digital-asset trading and technology firm that delivers liquidity, execution, and market infrastructure to token issuers, exchanges, and institutions. It is a regulated Crypto-Asset Service Provider registered with France's AMF and licensed by Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA). Products span liquidity solutions (token, stablecoin, exchange, and DeFi), OTC trading (spot, derivatives, and credit) across 150+ venues and 1,000+ asset pairs, tokenized-market infrastructure, and ventures. Flowdesk exposes a developer-facing "Platform Connect" API for programmatic OTC spot trading over REST with a companion WebSocket streaming channel, authenticated with OAuth 2.0 JWT bearer tokens issued through its Auth0 tenant.

providers.name: Inscope
providers.description: Inscope is an AI-powered financial reporting and automation platform for accounting firms and enterprise finance teams. It drafts accurate, GAAP-compliant financial statements, cash flow statements, and audit workpapers in minutes, keeping a human reviewer in the loop to review and sign off. The platform targets the financial close, reporting, and audit workflow, and states SOC 2 Type I and Type II certification with GDPR/CCPA compliance. Inscope is a private SaaS backed by Norwest Venture Partners; it publishes no public product API or developer portal today. Customer sign-in runs on a PropelAuth-hosted OpenID Connect tenant at auth.inscopehq.com.

providers.name: IRALOGIX
providers.description: IRALOGIX is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania fintech that operates a cloud-native, white-label IRA (Individual Retirement Account) recordkeeping and administration platform for financial institutions — banks, wealth managers, brokerages, recordkeepers and advisors — who use it to offer digital IRA programs under their own brand. The platform covers onboarding, contributions, trading, distributions, rollovers, compliance monitoring and administration end to end, and the company markets "API-driven connectivity and real-time data flows" that integrate with existing custodial and recordkeeping infrastructure rather than replacing it. The developer surface is partner-gated: documentation at docs.iralogix.com sits behind Okta visitor authentication and the partner console at partner.iralogix.com behind an Auth0 tenant, so no public OpenAPI, AsyncAPI or SDK is published. The company states SSAE SOC 2 Type 1 and SSAE SOC 1 Type 2 attestation.

providers.name: OneBlinc
providers.description: OneBlinc is a US consumer fintech that provides cash advances, credit-building and financial-wellness products to public-sector, healthcare and other essential workers who are underserved by traditional banks. Its consumer products are delivered through the OneBlinc / BlincAdvance mobile apps — BlincAdvance (paycheck advances from $50 up to $250 on an $8.99/month subscription, with an optional paid instant-deposit tier), BlincBoost (a credit-building subscription), BlincShield and BlincEarn — and a legacy installment-loan product originated by BlincLoans, Inc. that is not currently accepting new applications. Its one business-facing product, BlincFy, sells customer-permissioned income and employment verification data and analytics, but is sold through a "Schedule a Demo" sales motion with no public developer documentation. OneBlinc publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or machine-readable specification; api.oneblinc.com is a private backend for its own mobile clients.

providers.name: Stack Health
providers.description: Stack Healthcare (stackhealthcare.com) is a health-insurance fintech offering affordable, flexible coverage for small businesses and their teams. Operating as a technology company rather than a bank, Stack acts as a HIPAA Business Associate to employer-sponsored health plans, processing Protected Health Information for enrollment and benefits administration, and partners with Stripe for payments and Celtic Bank for issuing commercial cards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of 8vc and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Stack publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface — the product is a waitlist-gated web application — so this profile captures the identity, security, and compliance posture that is publicly verifiable.

providers.name: Pontera
providers.description: Pontera (formerly FeeX; legal entity Pontera Solutions Inc.) is a wealthtech platform that lets financial advisors securely manage, rebalance, and report on clients' held-away workplace-sponsored retirement accounts — 401(k), 401(a), 403(b), 457, TSP, and certain 529 plans — without a rollover. Accounts connect through a client-permissioned, credential-free workflow designed to avoid triggering custody under SEC Rule 206(4)-2, with an un-editable audit log for supervision. Pontera integrates with portfolio-management, reporting, billing, and supervision systems (Orion, Addepar, Black Diamond, Morningstar and others) but publishes no public developer API. Backed by ICONIQ Capital and Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Better Mortgage
providers.description: Better (Better Home & Finance Company, operating as Better Mortgage) is a New York-based fintech founded in 2014 by Vishal Garg that digitizes home finance end to end. Its online platform originates purchase mortgages, refinances, home equity lines of credit (HELOC), and VA loans, and connects borrowers with title, closing, homeowners insurance (via Better Cover), and real-estate agent matching. Better was the first fintech to fund over $100 billion in home loans entirely online and markets an "AI-powered" One Day Mortgage experience. Better does not publish a general-purpose public developer API, but it operates a live OpenID Connect / OAuth 2.0 identity provider (backed by AWS Cognito) for partner single sign-on, discoverable at its /.well-known endpoints.

providers.name: Built
providers.description: Built (Built Technologies) is an AI-powered real estate and construction finance platform that connects capital and information across the construction lending ecosystem. It serves banks, credit unions, private credit firms, owners, developers, and general contractors with construction loan administration, deal origination and underwriting, project financials, invoice and lien-waiver management, compliance tracking, and payments. Founded over a decade ago and headquartered in Nashville and New York, Built operates on one of the largest connected datasets in real estate finance and integrates with Procore, Sage Intacct, Yardi, QuickBooks, Encompass, nCino, and DocuSign. It is backed by Fifth Wall and Index Ventures. This profile was enriched from Built's public developer and trust surfaces; Built publishes an integrations directory, identity/SSO, a status page, and a trust center, but does not expose a public REST API or OpenAPI.

providers.name: Finrep
providers.description: Finrep is an AI-powered financial reporting intelligence platform for the office of the CFO. It helps SEC reporting, technical accounting, legal counsel, investor relations, disclosure committee, internal audit, tax, and ESG teams research, benchmark, validate, and draft SEC disclosures grounded in EDGAR filings, authoritative accounting guidance (ASC/IFRS), and IR materials — with every answer traceable to inspectable source documents. Finrep ships 40+ purpose-built CFO-office workflows spanning comment-letter analysis, disclosure drafting, Section 16 filing, and peer benchmarking, and can deploy on-premises or in a private cloud. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Self
providers.description: Self (Self Financial, Inc.) is a fintech platform that helps people build credit, savings, and access to cash through a small set of consumer financial products. Its Credit Builder Account pairs a small installment loan with a locked savings deposit and reports on-time payments to all three major credit bureaus; the Self Secured Credit Card requires no credit check, and Rent & Bills Reporting and Self Cash round out the lineup. Self serves several million members and is a Techstars portfolio company. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public identity, security posture, and compliance certifications.

providers.name: Calypso Workstation
providers.description: Nasdaq Calypso Workstation is the user-facing desktop component of the Nasdaq Calypso (formerly Adenza / Calypso Technology) capital markets platform. It gives capital markets professionals access to market data, trading operations, risk management, and portfolio analytics across asset classes. The Workstation is an integrated client application rather than a publicly documented REST API; programmatic integration is delivered through the broader Calypso platform interfaces used by banks, asset managers, central banks, and clearing houses.

providers.name: Catena
providers.description: Catena (Catena Labs) is building a regulated banking and governance platform for AI agents. The platform gives agents verified identities, custodial and non-custodial accounts, fiat and stablecoin payment rails across ten chains, yield on idle assets, and policy-enforced spending controls. For the humans and businesses deploying those agents it is a control plane: set policy, cap spending, restrict counterparties, audit every movement, and halt activity when needed. Agents access the platform through an API, a CLI, an MCP server, and a Skills framework. Founded by Sean Neville (CEO) and Matt Venables (CTO) - both Circle co-founders and creators of USDC - Catena has filed for a National Trust Bank charter with the OCC and raised $48M total ($30M Series A co-led by a16z crypto and Acrew, with QED, Coinbase Ventures, General Catalyst, Breyer Capital, IDG Capital, Oak HC/FT, and Pillar).

providers.name: Tebi
providers.description: Tebi is a hospitality management platform that unifies point-of-sale, payments, and back-office operations for restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, quick-service venues, and events. The system connects front-of-house service to back-office administration in a single product spanning Point of Sale, Kitchen Display System, Reservations, integrated card Payments (with invoicing and split-bill), QR ordering, inventory management, CRM, recipe management, and AI-driven insights. Tebi is priced on a revenue-based subscription (the first EUR 10k of monthly revenue is free, each additional EUR 10k costs EUR 20/month) with no long-term contracts, and it bundles its own payment processing with transparent per-transaction fees. The company is backed by Index Ventures. Tebi does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; this profile captures its production identity, help center, changelog, status page, and security posture as surfaced by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Ylookup
providers.description: Ylookup is a London-based fintech (founded 2025, EQT Ventures-backed) building an agentic workflow engine for fund administration, corporate services, tax, audit, and deal advisory firms. Its platform embeds trusted AI agents into existing tools (Excel, PDFs, Investran, Paxus) as a centralized processing layer — no data migration required — with specialized agents for extracting data from financial documents (LPAs, debt agreements, KYC/AML and tax forms), real-time reconciliation across spreadsheets and sources, financial analysis, and four-eye review. The company reports an average 76% time saved across live processes such as fund-accounting migration, client onboarding, financial-statement preparation, and K-1 data extraction. Ylookup publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; this profile captures its identity and published security/compliance posture.

providers.name: Back Office
providers.description: Back Office, Inc. operates Finally (finally.com), a Miami-based fintech that provides a unified, AI-powered bookkeeping, accounting, and finance suite for growing small and medium-sized businesses. The platform combines automated bookkeeping and ledger management, accounts payable and bill pay, expense management, corporate cards with built-in controls, invoicing, payment processing, payroll across 150+ countries, and credit monitoring, with AI agents that classify transactions, reconcile accounts, close the books, and prepare audits. Founded in 2018 and trusted by over 3,500 companies, Finally publishes a SOC 2 trust center but does not currently expose a public developer API or developer portal; this profile tracks its identity, web properties, and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Boku
providers.description: Boku is a global mobile payments network that connects digital merchants to more than 200 local payment methods — mobile wallets, real-time account-to-account bank transfers, and direct carrier billing — across 70+ countries, reaching over 7 billion payment accounts. Through its Boku Direct payment gateway API, merchants such as Epic Games, Google, Meta, Microsoft, Netflix, Sony, Spotify, and Tencent accept local payments, run subscriptions, and settle globally. Boku processes over $9 billion in payments annually and is publicly traded on the London Stock Exchange (LON:BOKU).

providers.name: Concourse
providers.description: Concourse builds AI agents for corporate finance teams. Its platform lets finance, accounting, and data teams query financial data in natural language, generate board and investor reporting with commentary, and run forecasts and scenarios against real-time data. Concourse connects natively to financial and operational systems including QuickBooks, NetSuite, Ramp, Snowflake, Salesforce, HubSpot, Stripe, Brex, Rippling, Gusto, BigQuery, and Databricks, and says it cuts manual finance work by over 75%. The company is SOC 2 Type II certified and backed by CRV, raising a $12M Series A alongside general availability. This profile was surfaced from a VC portfolio and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: CrowdStreet
providers.description: Crowd Street (formerly CrowdStreet) is an online private-markets investing platform that gives accredited investors direct access to commercial real estate, private equity, venture capital, private credit, and real estate fund offerings. Founded in 2013 and headquartered in Austin, Texas, the company operates a marketplace where sponsors raise capital and members subscribe to individual deals, diversified funds, and managed portfolios, alongside an education center, glossary, and research library. Crowd Street Capital LLC is a FINRA-member broker-dealer and Crowd Street Advisors LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser. The platform is delivered as a members-only investor web application; as of this profile Crowd Street publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: LendingPad
providers.description: LendingPad is a cloud-based mortgage loan origination system (LOS) that lets brokers, lenders, and institutions originate, process, underwrite, close, and fund residential mortgage loans with real-time, multi-user collaboration across the borrower, broker, lender, and service-provider lifecycle. It ships in Broker, Lender, Processing, and Institution editions and runs a large Partners Marketplace of integrated vendors (credit, AUS, AVM/appraisal, title, compliance, doc-prep, pricing/PPE, POS, CRM, and investors such as Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, UWM, and Rocket Mortgage). LendingPad exposes an Enterprise API for loan data exchange, but access is gated - it is limited to Lender Edition clients under an executed API Agreement and NDA, keys and testing-site access are issued by the support desk, and there is no public developer portal or self-serve API reference. The API entries below are honestly modeled from the vendor-integration and marketplace capabilities LendingPad describes publicly; endpoint-level surfaces are not published and are not fabricated here.

providers.name: Nilus
providers.description: Nilus is an AI-powered treasury management platform ("your agentic workforce for treasury") that gives finance teams real-time cash visibility across banks, entities and currencies. Its modular platform pairs pre-built AI agents with connectivity to 20,000+ banks and payment service providers (via SWIFT, host-to-host and API) and major ERPs (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Dynamics 365) to automate reconciliation, cash-flow forecasting, payment workflows, FX exposure tracking, debt-covenant monitoring and idle-cash investment. Founded in 2021 by Daniel Kalish (ex-PayPal) and Danielle Shaul (ex-Fundbox), Nilus is based in New York with a Tel Aviv presence, is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Felicis and Vesey Ventures, and serves customers including Alloy, Taboola, Made In Cookware and Planned Parenthood. Nilus operates as a closed B2B SaaS and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI contract or developer portal.

providers.name: PrimeRevenue
providers.description: PrimeRevenue is a global financial technology company providing working capital and B2B payment solutions through a bank-agnostic, ERP-integrated platform. Its offerings include Supply Chain Finance (buyers extend payment terms while suppliers are paid early), Receivables Finance (suppliers sell invoices for early payment without buyer disclosure), Dynamic Discounting (early payment at variable discount rates), and Payments as a Service (a modern B2B payment layer). The platform manages more than $25B in daily assets, has accelerated over 12.5M invoices, and supports 30+ languages. PrimeRevenue does not publish a public developer portal or API documentation; this profile captures its corporate, security, and compliance surface. Backed by Battery Ventures.

providers.name: Bstow
providers.description: Bstow is a fintech-for-good startup whose flagship product, Cheerful Giving, lets nonprofits and their supporters raise money through spare-change round-up donations, recurring gifts, and branded campaign pages. Backed by 500 Global, Bstow's Cheerful Giving product now operates as part of the Goodworld social-impact platform (goodworldnow.com), which layers on giving forms, events, peer-to-peer and workplace/payroll giving, text engagement, and an impact CRM. The platform documents webhooks and partner integrations (Salesforce, Stripe, PayPal, Klaviyo, Zapier, Fundraise Up) but does not publish a public, self-serve API reference or OpenAPI specification; API access is arranged directly with the vendor through a sales-gated developer portal. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Monnai
providers.description: Monnai is a global consumer-insights infrastructure company that delivers real-time, AI-ready data for decisioning across the entire customer lifecycle. Its Insights API unifies fragmented identity, device, phone, email, and behavioral signals from a proprietary data consortium into clean, contextual 360-degree profiles, enabling financial institutions, fintechs, ecommerce, and marketplaces to power acquisition, onboarding (KYC/AML), risk assessment and fraud detection, credit decisioning, and collections. Monnai provides localized coverage across 190+ countries with a privacy-first, encryption-backed approach. The API is secured with OAuth 2.0. Monnai is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: AccessFintech
providers.description: AccessFintech operates Synergy, a post-trade data and workflow network for capital markets that connects buy-side firms, broker-dealers, custodians, hedge funds, order management systems and vendors onto a shared view of trade, settlement and collateral data. The platform normalizes fragmented data across securities, derivatives and alternatives, detects breaks and exceptions across counterparties, and lets the parties to a trade resolve them collaboratively on a single record instead of by email and reconciliation files. AccessFintech describes Synergy as API-first, with bi-directional integrations, ingestion of JSON, XML, CSV and delimited text over push or pull, and Snowflake-native data sharing on AWS. The API surface is not self-serve: the Synergy application and its GraphQL and REST endpoints sit behind an Okta-backed customer login at login.accessfintech.com, and no public developer portal, reference or machine-readable specification is published.

providers.name: Alkami
providers.description: Alkami Technology (NASDAQ: ALKT) is a Plano, Texas based cloud digital banking platform for U.S. banks and credit unions. Through its "Alkami Foundry" developer program it exposes RESTful APIs and an extensible SDK — spanning authentication, money movement, data access, and real-time and batch workflows — that financial institutions and fintech partners use to embed and extend digital-banking experiences. The APIs are grouped into D2C (embed fintech experiences), B2B (automate backend workflows), and Open Banking (third-party connections such as Plaid) surfaces, are built on OpenID Connect, and are delivered through a gated DevPortal rather than an open public API. Alkami was surfaced as a portfolio company of D1 Capital and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from its public developer, security, and legal surfaces.

providers.name: Linker Finance
providers.description: Linker Finance Inc is a US financial technology company providing a digital banking and CRM platform for community and regional retail and commercial banks. Its platform covers digital account opening with embedded KYC and fraud checks, business and commercial onboarding with KYB, AML and beneficial-owner KYC, retail digital banking, and commercial banking features including positive pay, treasury management, remote deposit capture, team management and payment approvals. The platform runs on AWS, ships as responsive web plus native iOS and Android apps published under the bank's own app store accounts, and integrates with bank core systems directly or through integration partners. Linker Finance is a certified PREMIUM partner on the Fiserv AppMarket. Backed by Techstars and Alloy Labs, the company raised a $5M seed round. It publishes no public developer portal or API; its "API Connectivity" is a partner- and customer-scoped integration capability rather than an open API program.

providers.name: Traive
providers.description: Traive is a Brazilian agri-fintech that connects agribusiness with financial investors, using AI and data analytics to simplify credit access in the agricultural sector. Its Traive Agro product handles agricultural credit commercialization with risk analysis, process automation, and financing access, while Traive Finance provides credit risk analysis and access to qualified agricultural assets with traceability. The platform serves 160K+ registered producers and manages over R$6B in structured recurring credit operations. Traive publishes no public developer API; its platform authenticates via a Keycloak OpenID Connect provider whose public discovery documents reveal an internal service estate (credit, farmers, retailers, ERP integration, GraphQL) captured in this profile.

providers.name: Papaya Pay
providers.description: Papaya Payments is a Los Angeles based fintech that operates a mobile-first digital billing and bill-pay platform. Businesses in healthcare, government and municipalities, utilities, insurance, field services, and debt collection use Papaya to let their customers pay bills by photographing a paper statement or scanning a QR code and paying over SMS, email, or the Papaya iOS and Android apps, with no account or login required. Papaya advertises a Quickpay embeddable payment widget for paper-statement and portal integrations, and states that more than 2.5 million Americans have used the service. The company markets PCI, HIPAA, and SOC2 compliance. As of this profile Papaya publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or API specification; it is a consumer-facing payments product rather than a developer platform. Backed by Bessemer Venture Partners.

providers.name: Bankjoy
providers.description: Bankjoy is an end-to-end digital banking platform purpose-built for community banks and credit unions. Founded in 2014 and based in the Detroit metro area (Royal Oak, Michigan), the Y Combinator- and Bessemer-backed fintech delivers consumer and business online and mobile banking, online account opening, online loan origination, digital statements, and fraud tooling (FraudSense) to 85+ financial institutions serving more than one million members. Bankjoy's API-based technology integrates with banking cores including Corelation KeyStone (as its first Certified Partner) and Fiserv, plus 150+ partner integrations. It is a business-to-business SaaS provider and does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: dv01
providers.description: dv01 is an "InvestorTech" data and analytics platform for the structured finance and consumer-lending markets, part of Fitch Group. It aggregates, standardizes, and validates loan-level data across asset classes (RMBS, auto, student loans, personal loans, buy-now-pay-later) and delivers it, along with reporting and surveillance tooling, to issuers, lenders, and investors. Products include Data Direct, Data Management, DealStudio, Securitizations, Tape Cracker, and portfolio/market surveillance. dv01 publishes no public developer REST API or OpenAPI; data is delivered into client environments via Snowflake Data Share, BigQuery, SFTP, and S3. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Ribbit Capital and enriched with verified public identity, compliance, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Forecastr
providers.description: Forecastr is a startup financial planning and forecasting platform, founded in 2018 in Louisville, Kentucky, that helps founders and finance teams build investor-ready financial models, track cash flow and runway, plan headcount, budget expenses, and run what-if scenario analysis. It pairs cloud-based forecasting software (a spreadsheet-style formula builder, pre-built templates, drag-and-drop dashboards, and shareable live models) with fractional CFO services, and keeps actuals current through accounting integrations with QuickBooks Online and Xero. Forecastr is an API consumer of those accounting platforms rather than a public API provider; it publishes no developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Fullseam
providers.description: FullSeam builds AI agents for corporate accounting and finance operations teams, automating the manual work that happens outside traditional accounting software. Its agents handle accounts receivable (following up on payments, generating requested documentation, and entering invoices into customer AP portals), accounts payable (extracting invoices from multiple sources, matching them against purchase orders and contracts, chasing vendors for missing information, and categorizing expenses before posting to the general ledger), cash application, and reconciliation. FullSeam integrates with existing systems including QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Sage, Bill, Stripe, HubSpot, Salesforce, and PandaDoc rather than requiring a platform migration, flagging exceptions with full context for human review and maintaining audit logs for compliance. Founded by the team behind TaxProper (acquired by Opendoor), FullSeam is a Y Combinator Winter 2026 company.

providers.name: Fundera
providers.description: Fundera by NerdWallet is a small business financial guidance and lending marketplace platform that helps small business owners compare and access loan products, business credit cards, checking accounts, and financial health tools. Fundera connects borrowers with a vetted network of lenders offering SBA loans, term loans, lines of credit, equipment financing, invoice factoring, merchant cash advances, and commercial real estate loans. Acquired by NerdWallet in 2020, Fundera has secured over $5.4 billion in funds for more than 77,000 small businesses.

providers.name: Indifi
providers.description: Indifi Technologies Pvt. Ltd. is an Indian digital lending platform that provides collateral-free business loans to micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Founded in Gurugram, Indifi originates and underwrites term loans, working-capital lines of credit, unsecured lines of credit, invoice discounting, and merchant cash advances (against POS transaction history), funding them through a network of 15+ RBI-regulated NBFCs and banks as well as its own NBFC, Indifi Capital Pvt. Ltd. (RBI Cert. No. B-14.03389). Loans range up to INR 50 lakhs with tenures up to 36 months and rates from 1.5% per month, assessed largely on business cash-flow, GST, and platform transaction data rather than traditional collateral. Indifi works through industry partnerships with e-commerce marketplaces and sector aggregators and through co-lending/DSA lending partners; it does not currently publish a public developer API or portal. Backed by Accel.

providers.name: Neobanks
providers.description: A collection of APIs from leading neobanks and digital banking platforms including Revolut, Monzo, Starling Bank, N26, Nubank, Bunq, and others that offer modern banking services through developer-friendly APIs.

providers.name: Origin Financial
providers.description: Origin (Blend Financial Inc. DBA Origin Financial) is a personal finance platform built around an SEC-regulated AI financial advisor, combining spending tracking, budgeting, investing, tax filing, estate planning, and couples money management in one app, and offering employers a financial wellness benefit. Account connections run through partners including Plaid, MX, and Mastercard. Origin is a consumer and employer product with no public developer API surface today.

providers.name: Prism Data
providers.description: Prism Data is a cash flow underwriting infrastructure and analytics platform that helps lenders expand approvals and lower losses by turning raw bank transaction data into decisioning signals. Its products include CashScore (a cash-flow-based credit score), transaction Categories, Income verification, and Insights, delivered through an API and the Pulse dashboard for credit underwriting across the United States and Canada. Developer API documentation is published at docs.prismdata.com behind a developer login.

providers.name: Figure Markets
providers.description: Figure Markets is a blockchain-native digital-asset marketplace built on the Provenance Blockchain that lets individuals and institutions trade, borrow against, and earn yield on crypto and real-world assets from a single account. Its exchange runs on Connamara's EP3 matching engine with FIX and REST APIs, offering a central limit order book for crypto (BTC, ETH, and more), equities, bonds, alternative assets, and YLDS, the first SEC-registered yielding stablecoin. Products include Figure Exchange (pro trading), crypto-backed loans, Democratized Prime (HELOC-backed yield), and self-custodied wallets, bridging traditional order-book finance with on-chain clearing and settlement. The company is backed by DCM Ventures. The trading API is served from api.figuremarkets.com and is access-controlled; no public OpenAPI is currently published.

providers.name: Maxima
providers.description: Maxima is an AI-native accounting and financial-close automation platform for enterprise finance teams. Its AI agents automate the core work of the accounting close — journal entries, cash coding, payroll entries, bank and balance-sheet reconciliations, flux (variance) analysis, and fixed-asset depreciation — while connecting natively to the systems finance teams already use (the company advertises 150+ integrations across ERPs, banks, and payroll providers). Maxima is an early-stage, enterprise-focused company backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this pass the company runs a corporate marketing site and a gated web application (app.maximahq.com) and does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Investly
providers.description: Investly is a European fintech invoice-financing marketplace that helps growing small and medium-sized businesses unlock working capital by financing their outstanding 30-180 day invoices. Businesses sell their approved invoices through a reverse-auction marketplace where investors bid to fund them, giving merchants the best available price from multiple funding providers and access to cash in 1-3 working days rather than waiting on customer payment terms. Founded by Siim Maivel and operating across Estonia and the United Kingdom, Investly is backed by Speedinvest, Startup Wise Guys, and Founders Capital. The platform serves established businesses across manufacturing, wholesale, construction, logistics, and business-services sectors and has funded invoices worth tens of millions of pounds to date. Investly runs a production HAL/HATEOAS backend API at api.investly.co, though it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or API reference documentation.

providers.name: Xepelin
providers.description: Xepelin is a Chilean-founded fintech operating in Chile and Mexico that provides digital financial services for small and mid-sized businesses, including invoice factoring (adelanto de facturas), supplier payment financing (confirming), working capital credit lines, and collections and payments management, alongside XData, a financial-intelligence product for evaluating clients and suppliers. The company reports more than 60,000 business customers and over five billion USD financed in the last three years, with digital credit approval in under 24 hours. Xepelin does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation.

providers.name: AstroPay
providers.description: AstroPay is a Uruguay-founded fintech and electronic money institution offering a multicurrency wallet, virtual and physical AstroCards, FX, and cross-border money transfers for consumers across Latin America, plus a business platform that lets merchants accept payments, issue cards, manage payroll, and pay out to wallets and bank accounts. AstroPay is regulated as an EMI in the UK, Denmark, Isle of Man, and Brazil, and operates the AstroPay wallet across Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Peru, Colombia, Uruguay, and additional global corridors with support for ARS, BRL, CLP, COP, EUR, GBP, MXN, PEN, USD, USDT, and UYU. For developers, AstroPay exposes a comprehensive REST platform spanning payments, payouts, PIX instant payments in Brazil, issued cards, savings accounts, scheme transfers, user account management, tokenization (PCI-compliant card collection), settlements, transaction reporting, hosted and embedded Checkout, QR-code POS, Wallet-on-File account linking, Cashouts, and Webhooks — accessed through `developers.astropay.com` with HMAC-signed callbacks and an OAuth/API-key authentication model.

providers.name: Metric
providers.description: Metric is an AI-powered financial intelligence and accounting platform built for business owners, founders, and CEOs. It replaces spreadsheets and expensive CFO teams with a real-time financial dashboard and Max, an AI co-pilot (CF-AI) that answers financial questions such as runway, hiring capacity, and spending in plain language, drawn from live financial data. Metric handles accounting and bookkeeping, payables and receivables, invoicing, eight report types, and UAE VAT compliance, and connects to QuickBooks, Zoho Books, Xero, and Shopify. Headquartered in Abu Dhabi with offices in Rawalpindi, Singapore, and Riyadh, it is backed by 500 Global and serves businesses across 190+ countries. Metric is a SaaS web application with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Roofstock
providers.description: Roofstock is a residential real estate investment platform and online marketplace for buying, selling, and managing single-family rental (SFR) homes. It gives individual and institutional investors research, analytics, certified property listings, and end-to-end services spanning acquisitions, property management (Mynd), portfolio accounting software (Stessa), tenant screening (RentPrep), asset management, and dispositions across dozens of U.S. markets. The company reports hundreds of thousands of users and over $10B in transacted volume. Roofstock operates a private web API (api.roofstock.com) and a GraphQL endpoint powering its marketplace applications; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, first-party SDKs, or documented API access. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and SoftBank Vision Fund and enriched from Roofstock's public web surface.

providers.name: Anduin
providers.description: Anduin (Anduin Transactions) is a private-markets technology company that digitizes investor onboarding and fund operations for venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds. Its platform replaces paper-based subscription workflows with electronic fund subscription documents, secure data rooms, investor data management, an engagement hub, an integration hub, automated data extraction, and e-signature. The company reports 1,305+ funds served, $244B+ capital raised, and 74,000+ investors subscribed. Anduin publishes no public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile captures its public company, trust, and security surfaces (Trust Center, RFC 9116 security.txt, and domain-security posture). Backed by 8vc; surfaced to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: Ava
providers.description: Ava is a consumer financial-technology company that helps people build credit and reduce the cost of debt. Its products include the Ava Credit Builder Mastercard (a no-interest card usable at approved subscription merchants), a Save & Build secured savings loan, and rent and utility payment reporting to the three major U.S. credit bureaus (TransUnion, Equifax, Experian). Ava operates as a mobile app on a subscription model and partners with regulated banks and lenders (including Patriot Bank, N.A. and Pier Lending) to deliver its products. This profile was surfaced as a Greylock portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Ava is a consumer app and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Duco
providers.description: Duco is an AI-powered operational data automation platform for financial services. It helps banks, asset managers, brokers, asset servicers and market infrastructure firms normalize, validate and reconcile any data in the cloud — cutting the time spent on manual data work, reducing operational risk and accelerating front-, middle- and back-office processes. The no-code platform ingests data from any source (including unstructured documents via Adaptive Intelligent Document Processing), then transforms, matches, reconciles and publishes it with full audit and control. Duco's Agentic Workspace layers agentic AI over these operations so agents can handle repetitive extraction, matching and exception-labelling work under human oversight. Use cases span securities and derivatives reconciliation, ETD clearing, OTC confirmations, custody, cash accounts, crypto holdings and transaction/regulatory reporting (EMIR, CFTC, MiFID II, ASIC, MAS, T+1). Customers include HSBC, Deutsche Bank, ING, Santander, Northern Trust and Fidelity Digital Assets. Duco is backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Fifteenth
providers.description: Fifteenth is a San Francisco-based fintech company operating an AI-powered personal tax platform for ambitious earners — founders, investors, executives, and technology professionals with complex financial situations such as equity compensation (ISOs, RSOs, RSUs, NSOs), liquidity events (IPOs and acquisitions), partnership income (K-1s), and active stock and crypto trading. The service pairs dedicated human CPAs with AI-driven automation: users link their banking, payroll, and investment accounts via one-click integrations (Workday, Rippling, Robinhood, Wealthfront, Carta, Charles Schwab, AngelList, Coinbase and more), and the platform automatically detects tax-relevant transactions, organizes documents, models scenarios, and delivers proactive quarterly planning plus unlimited year-round advice at flat-fee pricing starting around $1,000 per year. Fifteenth raised $8.25M in seed funding (February 2025) led by A* and General Catalyst. It is a consumer-facing product with no public developer API surface; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Palm
providers.description: Palm is an AI cash flow forecasting platform for corporate treasury and finance teams. It sits above existing Treasury Management Systems (TMS) and ERPs, unifying visibility across cash positions and forecasting liquidity directly from bank and transaction data. Palm learns the timing and size of recurring cash flows from historical transactions to keep a rolling 13-week-and-longer forecast current automatically, and combines ERP data, bank transactions, and 25+ AI models to improve forecast accuracy by over 60%. The product spans AI cash forecasting, what-if scenario modeling, continuous forecast-vs-actual variance analysis, automated daily cash positioning across banks and currencies, surplus-cash investment identification, board-ready treasury reporting, and a "Pulse" anomaly-detection assistant. Palm is a speedinvest portfolio company. It integrates with TMS (Coupa, FIS, ION, Kyriba), banks (Citi, HSBC, J.P. Morgan), investment platforms, data warehouses, and ERPs (SAP, IFS), but does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Fairplay
providers.description: Fairplay is a Mexican fintech offering flexible, collateral-free business financing for e-commerce sellers, marketplaces, retailers, and wholesalers. Its products include revolving credit lines (MXN 2-30 million), invoice advances/factoring, and working-capital financing, underwritten from a company's sales and analytics data with offers issued in as little as 48 hours through a 100% digital process. Fairplay operates as a Sociedad Financiera de Objeto Multiple, Entidad No Regulada (SOFOM E.N.R.) under Mexican CNBV and CONDUSEF supervision and is ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified for information security. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of QED Investors and Speedinvest. Fairplay serves financing and account data to customers through a private insights dashboard; no public developer API is currently published.

providers.name: Frete.com
providers.description: Frete.com is the Brazilian road-freight technology group formed in January 2023 when CargoX merged with Fretebras and FretePago, becoming Latin America's largest freight-matching platform and one of Brazil's logistics unicorns after a US$200M round led by SoftBank and Tencent. The group operates three consumer-facing brands: Fretebras, the freight marketplace that connects shippers and carriers with autonomous truck drivers; CargoX Brasil, which bundles working-capital credit, cargo insurance, document issuance and truck tracking for trucking companies; and FretePago, a fintech offering a digital account and freight payment rails for drivers and fleets. It also acquired Rotas Brasil for route mapping and toll pricing. The platform applies machine learning to freight matching, fraud and cargo-theft prevention, and pricing intelligence. Frete.com does not currently publish a public developer portal or machine-readable API contract; the Fretebras integration API is reached through partner and ERP/TMS channels rather than an open reference.

providers.name: GetGoing
providers.description: GetGoing is a cloud-based corporate travel and expense (T&E) management platform for small and midsize businesses, built and operated by BCD Travel. It combines self-service booking of flights, hotels, rental cars and rail with automated travel and expense policy enforcement, pre-trip approval flows, streamlined payments and invoicing, traveler safety and duty-of-care, and analytics dashboards in a single product that can be implemented in under two hours. GetGoing pairs the digital self-service experience with BCD Travel's global travel-management expertise and support, and is offered across the United States, United Kingdom, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Belgium.
